Option C splits the sample equally between the three groups, option B divides the group size by the sample size, and option D compares juniors with the other groups instead of with the total.

questions.question: In a grouped frequency distribution, two consecutive class midpoints are 14.5 and 24.5. What is the class width?
questions.explanation: With equal class widths, consecutive midpoints are exactly one class width apart, so width = 24.5 - 14.5 = 10. Option A averages the midpoints, option B subtracts 1 as if working with limits, and option D halves the gap.

questions.question: For whole-number data, a class has a midpoint of 44.5 and a class width of 10. What are its class LIMITS?
questions.explanation: The boundaries are 44.5 -/+ 5, i.e. 39.5 and 49.5; for whole-number data the limits are 0.5 inside the boundaries, giving 40-49. Option A gives the boundaries rather than the limits, and options C and D wrongly treat the midpoint as an end of the class.

questions.question: Data range from a lowest value of 12 to a highest value of 71 (whole numbers). If classes of width 10 are used, starting with the class 10-19, how many classes are needed to cover all the data?
questions.explanation: The classes are 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59, 60-69 and 70-79; the highest value 71 falls in 70-79, so 7 classes are needed. Option A stops at 60-69 and leaves out 71, option B divides the range (59) by 10 and rounds down, and option C adds an unnecessary extra class.

questions.question: The arithmetic mean of 4, 8, 6, 10, 12 is:
questions.explanation: The mean is the sum of the values divided by how many there are: (4 + 8 + 6 + 10 + 12) / 5 = 40 / 5 = 8. The other options come from adding or dividing incorrectly; for example, 10 (D) would need a total of 50.

questions.question: Which of the following measures is least affected by extreme values (outliers) in a data set?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value of the ranked data, so one very large or very small value hardly moves it. The mean (A) is pulled towards extreme values because every value enters the total, while the range (B) and variance (C) depend heavily on the most extreme values.

questions.question: The standard deviation is calculated as:

options.b: The square root of the variance

questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of the variance, which brings the measure of spread back to the original units of the data. Squaring the variance (A) goes the wrong way, and the mean (C) and half the range (D) are different measures altogether.

questions.question: A coefficient of correlation of r = -0.9 indicates:
questions.explanation: The negative sign shows that as one variable rises the other falls, and a value of 0.9, close to 1, shows the relationship is strong. Option A ignores the negative sign, option B would need r close to 0, and option D would need a value much nearer to 0, such as -0.2.

questions.question: In a normal distribution, approximately what percentage of observations fall within +/-1 standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation: By the empirical rule, about 68% of observations lie within one standard deviation either side of the mean. About 95% (C) lie within two standard deviations and about 99.7% (D) within three, while 50% (A) is the share on each side of the mean.

questions.question: The coefficient of determination is given by:
questions.explanation: The coefficient of determination is r squared, which shows the proportion of the variation in y that is explained by x. The plain correlation coefficient r (A) measures strength and direction, while 1/r (C) and the square root of r (D) have no standard meaning here.

questions.question: The Upper Control Limit on a standard control chart is typically set at:
questions.explanation: Standard control charts set the UCL at the process mean plus three standard deviations, and the LCL at the mean minus three. Limits at one or two standard deviations (A and B) would flag too many false alarms, and multiplying the mean by 3 (D) is not how control limits work.

questions.question: If two data sets have the same mean but different standard deviations, the set with the larger standard deviation is:
questions.explanation: A larger standard deviation means the values are scattered further from the mean, so that data set is more spread out and less consistent. Options A and B describe the set with the smaller standard deviation, and option D contradicts the different standard deviations.

questions.question: The slope (b) in a simple linear regression equation represents:

options.b: The average rate of change in y for a one-unit change in x

questions.explanation: In y-hat = a + bx, the slope b shows how much y changes, on average, when x increases by one unit. The y-intercept (A) is a, the value of y when x is zero, and the correlation coefficient (C) is a separate measure, r.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a measure of dispersion?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequently occurring value, so it is a measure of central tendency, not of spread. The range (A), standard deviation (B) and variance (D) all describe how widely the data are scattered.

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of r = 0 suggests:
questions.explanation: An r of 0 means there is no linear relationship between the two variables. A perfect positive relationship (A) would be r = +1, a perfect negative one (B) would be r = -1, and a strong relationship (D) needs r close to +1 or -1.

questions.question: The mode of a data set is:
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often in a data set. The middle value (A) is the median, the average (B) is the mean, and the largest value (D) is the maximum.

questions.question: A company wants a single figure for the "typical" salary of its staff, but a few directors earn far more than everyone else. Which measure is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: The median is the middle value of the ranked salaries, so the few very high director salaries do not drag it upwards. The mean (B) would be pulled up by those extreme values, while the range (C) and standard deviation (A) measure spread rather than a typical value.

questions.question: For the data 5, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 40, which statement is correct (mean to 1 decimal place)?
questions.explanation: The mean is 86 / 7 = 12.3, the median is the 4th of the 7 ranked values, which is 8, and the mode is 7 because it appears twice. The other options mix up the three measures; notice also that the outlier 40 pulls the mean above the median.

questions.question: Which formula gives the coefficient of variation (CV)?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of variation is the standard deviation expressed as a percentage of the mean, which measures relative dispersion and allows sets with different means or units to be compared. Option A turns the ratio upside down, while options B and C use variance or range instead of standard deviation.

questions.question: Investment A has a mean return of 20% with a standard deviation of 4%; Investment B has a mean return of 10% with a standard deviation of 3%. Using CV = (SD / mean) x 100%, which investment has the lower relative risk?

options.b: B, with a CV of 20% against 30% for A
options.c: B, because its standard deviation is lower
options.d: A, with a CV of 20% against 30% for B

questions.explanation: CV for A = 4 / 20 x 100 = 20% and CV for B = 3 / 10 x 100 = 30%, so A has less risk per unit of return. Option C compares standard deviations only, which is misleading when the means differ, and option B swaps the two CVs.

questions.question: Which statement best distinguishes correlation from regression analysis?

options.a: Correlation proves causation, while regression does not
options.b: Both only measure the strength of a relationship and cannot be used for prediction
options.c: Regression measures the strength and direction of a relationship; correlation fits a line used for prediction
options.d: Correlation measures the strength and direction of a linear relationship; regression fits a line that can be used to predict one variable from the other

questions.explanation: Correlation gives a single number, r, describing how strong and in what direction a linear relationship is, while regression goes further by fitting a line such as y-hat = a + bx for prediction. Option C swaps the two, option B ignores the predictive use of regression, and correlation never proves causation (A).

questions.question: According to the empirical rule, approximately what percentage of observations in a normal distribution lie within +/-2 standard deviations of the mean?
questions.explanation: The empirical rule says about 68% of values lie within one standard deviation, about 95% within two, and about 99.7% within three. So 68% (D) and 99.7% (C) belong to one and three standard deviations, and 50% (B) is simply the half on each side of the mean.

questions.question: Test scores are normally distributed with a mean of 60 and a standard deviation of 5. Using the empirical rule, approximately what percentage of scores lie between 45 and 75?
questions.explanation: 45 and 75 are each 15 marks, or 3 standard deviations, away from the mean of 60, and about 99.7% of values lie within +/-3 standard deviations. Option D would apply to 50-70 (two standard deviations), and option C to 55-65 (one standard deviation).

questions.question: Which of the following is a managerial use of a control chart?

options.a: To detect when a production process has drifted outside acceptable limits
options.c: To find the critical path of a project
options.d: To calculate the economic order quantity

questions.explanation: A control chart plots measurements over time against upper and lower limits, so managers can spot when a process drifts out of control and separate random variation from real problems. EOQ (D), the critical path (C) and the break-even point (B) are found with other tools.

questions.question: Ice-cream sales and drowning incidents are found to be strongly positively correlated. Which is the best explanation?

options.a: Drowning incidents cause ice-cream sales to rise
options.b: A third variable, hot weather, increases both
options.d: The correlation coefficient must have been calculated wrongly

questions.explanation: Correlation measures association, not cause and effect; here hot weather is a lurking variable that pushes up both ice-cream sales and swimming, and so drownings. Options C and A wrongly assume one variable causes the other, and a genuine correlation can exist without either causing the other, so the calculation need not be wrong (D).

questions.question: For the data 14, 9, 21, 17, 11, 19, what are the range and the mean (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Range = highest - lowest = 21 - 9 = 12, and the mean = 91 / 6 = 15.17. Option B gives the highest value instead of the range, option C divides the total by 5 instead of 6, and option D adds the highest and lowest values instead of subtracting.

questions.question: In the regression line y-hat = a + bx, what does a represent?

options.a: The intercept: the predicted value of y when x = 0
options.b: The predicted value of the dependent variable
options.c: The slope: the change in y for a one-unit change in x
options.d: The value of the independent variable

questions.explanation: The constant a is the intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis, giving the predicted y when x is zero. The slope is b (C), the independent variable is x (D), and the predicted value of the dependent variable is y-hat itself (B).

questions.question: A regression line is y-hat = 19.5 + 2.93x, where x is advertising spend and y-hat is predicted sales (both in N'000). What are the predicted sales when x = 20?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 20: y-hat = 19.5 + 2.93 x 20 = 19.5 + 58.6 = 78.1, or about N78,100. Option B forgets to add the intercept, option A just adds a and b, and option D multiplies (a + b) by 20.

questions.question: The test scores of 8 management trainees are 62, 75, 58, 80, 70, 65, 90, 72. What is the mean score?
questions.explanation: The scores add up to 572, and 572 / 8 = 71.5. Option D is the median (the average of the 4th and 5th ranked values, 70 and 72), option A is halfway between the lowest and highest scores, and option B divides by 7 instead of 8.

questions.question: The test scores of 8 trainees are 62, 75, 58, 80, 70, 65, 90, 72. Treating them as a population (variance = sum of squared deviations / n), what is the variance?
questions.explanation: The mean is 71.5, the squared deviations add up to 744, and the population variance = 744 / 8 = 93.00. Option D divides by n - 1 = 7 (the sample formula), option A is the standard deviation, and option C is the sum of squared deviations before dividing.

questions.question: The test scores of 8 trainees are 62, 75, 58, 80, 70, 65, 90, 72. Treating them as a population (divide by n), what is the standard deviation to 2 decimal places?
questions.explanation: The population variance is 744 / 8 = 93, and the standard deviation is the square root of 93, which is 9.64. Option C uses the sample formula (dividing by 7), option A is the variance itself, and option D takes the square root twice.

questions.question: For 6 sales representatives, years of experience (x) and monthly sales (y, N'000) are: (1, 28), (2, 35), (3, 40), (5, 52), (6, 58), (8, 70). Using b = [n(sum xy) - (sum x)(sum y)] / [n(sum x^2) - (sum x)^2], what is the slope b to 2 decimal places?
questions.explanation: With sum x = 25, sum y = 283, sum xy = 1,386 and sum x^2 = 139, b = (6 x 1,386 - 25 x 283) / (6 x 139 - 625) = 1,241 / 209 = 5.94. Option C simply divides sum xy by sum x^2, option A turns the fraction upside down, and option B is the intercept a, not the slope.

questions.question: For 6 sales representatives, years of experience (x) and monthly sales (y, N'000) give the regression line y-hat = 22.43 + 5.94x. What are the predicted monthly sales for a representative with 10 years of experience (to 1 decimal place)?
questions.explanation: Substitute x = 10: y-hat = 22.43 + 5.94 x 10 = 22.43 + 59.4 = 81.8, or about N81,800. Option C leaves out the intercept, option B wrongly uses the mean of y (47.17) in place of the intercept, and option A is just the observed sales of the representative with 8 years.

questions.question: Which of the following is a main property of the normal distribution?

options.a: It is a symmetrical, bell-shaped curve with mean, median and mode equal at the centre
options.b: The total area under the curve equals 2
options.c: It is skewed to the right, so the mean is greater than the median
options.d: The mode lies at the far left of the curve

questions.explanation: The normal curve is symmetrical and bell-shaped, so the mean, median and mode all sit together at the centre. A right-skewed curve (C) is not normal, the total area under the curve is 1 or 100% (B), and the mode is at the centre, not the edge (D).

questions.question: The total area under a normal distribution curve is equal to:

options.d: It depends on the standard deviation

questions.explanation: The area under the normal curve represents all possible observations, so it always totals 1, or 100%. Half of that, 0.5 (C), lies on each side of the mean, 0.68 (A) is the area within one standard deviation, and the total does not change with the standard deviation (D), which only alters the shape.

questions.question: Team A's weekly sales (N'000) are 50, 52, 48, 51, 49 and Team B's are 30, 60, 70, 40, 50; both average 50. Using population standard deviation (divide by n), which statement is correct?

options.a: Team A has a standard deviation of about 1.41, so it is more consistent than Team B
options.b: Team B has a standard deviation of about 1.41, so it is more consistent than Team A
options.c: Team A has a standard deviation of about 14.14, so it is less consistent than Team B
options.d: Both teams are equally consistent because they have the same mean

questions.explanation: Team A's squared deviations add up to 10, so its SD is the square root of 10 / 5, about 1.41, while Team B's add up to 1,000, giving an SD of about 14.14. So Team A is far more consistent; options B and C swap the figures, and option D wrongly assumes that the same mean means the same spread.

questions.question: Team B's weekly sales (N'000) are 30, 60, 70, 40, 50, with a mean of 50 and a population standard deviation of about 14.14. Using CV = (SD / mean) x 100%, what is Team B's coefficient of variation (to 1 decimal place)?
questions.explanation: CV = 14.14 / 50 x 100 = 28.3%, so the variation is a little over a quarter of the average weekly sales. Option D is Team A's CV (1.41 / 50), option C is just the standard deviation, and option A divides the mean by the standard deviation instead.

questions.question: A filling process has a mean of 50 mm and a standard deviation of 0.4 mm. Using control limits of mean +/- 3 standard deviations, what are the UCL and LCL?
questions.explanation: UCL = 50 + 3 x 0.4 = 51.2 mm and LCL = 50 - 3 x 0.4 = 48.8 mm. Option D uses 2 standard deviations, option C uses only 1, and option A wrongly puts the lower limit at the mean.

questions.question: On a control chart, a sample measurement falls above the Upper Control Limit. How should management interpret this?

options.a: The control limits should simply be widened so the point fits
options.b: The process may be out of control because of a special cause, and should be investigated
options.c: The process is in statistical control, with only random variation present
options.d: The point should be ignored because it is above, not below, the limits

questions.explanation: Points within the limits suggest only random variation, but a point outside either limit signals that a special cause may be at work and the process should be investigated. Option C describes points inside the limits, widening the limits (A) would hide the problem, and points above the UCL matter just as much as those below the LCL (D).

questions.question: Correlation analysis measures:

options.c: The strength and direction of a linear relationship between two variables

questions.explanation: Correlation shows how strongly two variables move together in a straight-line pattern and whether they move in the same or opposite directions. Option A is the classic trap: correlation does not prove that one variable causes the other.

questions.question: The value of the correlation coefficient (r) ranges between:
questions.explanation: Pearson's r runs from -1 (perfect negative) through 0 (no linear relationship) to +1 (perfect positive). Option B would leave no room for negative relationships, which do occur, for example between price and demand.

questions.question: If advertising expenditure increases and sales also increase, this is an example of:
questions.explanation: When two variables move in the same direction, the correlation is positive. Option B would require sales to fall as advertising rises, and Option C describes a relationship studied while holding other variables constant.

questions.question: If price increases and quantity demanded decreases, this illustrates:
questions.explanation: Variables moving in opposite directions show negative correlation, as when a higher price leads to lower demand. Option B would need both to rise or fall together.

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of r = +1.0 indicates:
questions.explanation: r = +1.0 is the highest possible value and means all points lie exactly on an upward-sloping straight line, a perfect positive relationship. Option A is r = -1.0, and Option C is r = 0.

questions.question: On the usual interpretation scale for Pearson's r, a value between 0.7 and 0.9 indicates:
questions.explanation: Values of r from 0.7 to 0.9 are close to +1, so they show a strong positive relationship. Option D applies to middle values around 0.4 to 0.6, and Option A applies only to r = +1.0 exactly.

questions.question: Studying the relationship between only two variables (e.g. demand and supply), assuming a linear relationship, is called:
questions.explanation: Simple correlation looks at just one pair of variables. Option B involves three or more variables at once, and Option A studies two variables while holding others constant.

questions.question: Studying the relationship between crop yield and TWO factors, rainfall and chemical fertiliser, simultaneously (Y = a + b1x1 + b2x2) is an example of:
questions.explanation: When one variable is related to two or more others at the same time, the study is multiple correlation. Option C is limited to two variables only, and Option A would study yield against one factor while holding the other fixed.

questions.question: Studying the relationship between two variables while holding all other variables constant is called:
questions.explanation: Partial correlation isolates the link between one pair of variables by keeping the effect of the others fixed. Option B considers all the variables together without holding any constant, which is the opposite approach.

questions.question: Correlation in which the rate of change between two variables is constant is called:
questions.explanation: If one variable changes by a constant amount for each unit change in the other, the points follow a straight line and the correlation is linear. Option B applies when the rate of change varies, producing a curved pattern.

questions.question: On a scatter diagram, points falling exactly on an upward-sloping straight line represent:
questions.explanation: Points lying exactly on a rising straight line mean the variables move together perfectly, so r = +1, perfect positive correlation. Option A would need a downward-sloping line, and Option C would show no clear pattern.

questions.question: Which method is used to calculate correlation for ranked (ordinal) data?
questions.explanation: Spearman's rank correlation works on the ranks of the data, which makes it suitable for ordinal data such as rankings. Option C, Pearson's r, is meant for interval or ratio data measured on a numeric scale.

questions.question: A manager recorded advertising expenditure (x) and sales (y) over 5 months: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2, 4, 5, 8, 9. What is the sum of xy?
questions.explanation: Multiply each pair and add: (1 x 2) + (2 x 4) + (3 x 5) + (4 x 8) + (5 x 9) = 2 + 8 + 15 + 32 + 45 = 102. This sum is an input to Pearson's r, and it is not the same as multiplying the totals, (sum of x) x (sum of y) = 15 x 28 = 420; Options A, B and C come from adding the products wrongly.

questions.question: A manager recorded advertising expenditure (x) and sales (y) over 5 months: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2, 4, 5, 8, 9. What is the sum of x^2 (the sum of the squared x values)?
questions.explanation: Squaring each x value and adding gives 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 = 55, so C is correct. Options A (50), B (45) and D (60) come from slips in squaring or adding. Remember that the sum of x^2 is not the same as (sum of x)^2, which would be 15^2 = 225.

questions.question: A manager recorded advertising expenditure (x) and sales (y) over 5 months: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2, 4, 5, 8, 9. What is the sum of y^2 (the sum of the squared y values)?
questions.explanation: Squaring each y value gives 4, 16, 25, 64 and 81, which add up to 190, so C is correct. Options A (180), B (170) and D (200) are near misses from slips in squaring or adding. Also, the sum of y^2 is different from (sum of y)^2 = 28^2 = 784.

questions.question: A manager recorded advertising expenditure (x) and sales (y) over 5 months: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2, 4, 5, 8, 9. Pearson's correlation coefficient for this data is r = 0.988 (to 3 decimal places). This indicates:
questions.explanation: An r value close to +1 means the two variables move together very closely in the same direction, so B, a strong positive relationship, is correct. Option D would need r = -1 and option C would need a small negative r. Option A applies when r is close to 0, which is far from 0.988.

questions.question: A manager recorded advertising expenditure (x) and sales (y) over 5 months: x = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and y = 2, 4, 5, 8, 9. Using Pearson's formula r = [n(sum xy) - (sum x)(sum y)] / sqrt{[n(sum x^2) - (sum x)^2][n(sum y^2) - (sum y)^2]}, what is r? (Round to 3 decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Here n = 5, sum x = 15, sum y = 28, sum xy = 102, sum x^2 = 55 and sum y^2 = 190, so the numerator is 5(102) - 15(28) = 90 and the denominator is sqrt[(275 - 225)(950 - 784)] = sqrt(8,300) = 91.104, giving r = 0.988 (A). Option C (0.976) is r squared, not r, and option B (0.542) comes from dividing 90 by only one bracket (166) without the square root. Option D (1.800) is impossible because r always lies between -1 and +1.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a typical business application of correlation analysis?

options.a: Assisting in forecasting and business planning
options.b: Determining criminal liability in a court case
options.d: Studying the relationship between sales and advertising

questions.explanation: Correlation analysis measures how strongly two quantitative variables move together, which is why it is used for sales and advertising, price and demand, and forecasting and planning (options A, C and D). Determining criminal liability is a legal judgement about individual responsibility, not a measure of association between business variables, so B is the odd one out.

questions.question: Studying the relationship among ALL variables simultaneously, without holding any constant, is called:
questions.explanation: Total correlation studies the relationship among all the variables together, without holding any of them constant, so D is correct. Option B, partial correlation, does the opposite: it looks at two variables while the effect of the others is held constant. Option A, simple correlation, involves only two variables, and option C describes the shape of a relationship rather than how many variables are studied.

questions.question: Correlation in which the amount of change in one variable does NOT bear a constant ratio to the amount of change in the other variable is called:
questions.explanation: When the change in one variable does not bear a constant ratio to the change in the other, the points follow a curve rather than a straight line, which is non-linear (curvilinear) correlation, so D is correct. Option A, linear correlation, is the opposite case where the ratio of change is constant. Option B means no relationship at all, and option C is about holding other variables constant, not the shape of the relationship.

questions.question: Which author defined statistics as "the science of counting" and "the science of averages"?
questions.explanation: Defining statistics as the science of counting and also the science of averages is the classical definition given by Bowley, so D is correct. King (B) described statistics as a method of judging collective, natural and social phenomena from analysis or enumeration, while Boddington (C) called it the science of estimates and probabilities. Option A is not linked to this definition.

questions.question: Which author defined statistics as "the science of estimates and probabilities", used when counting is not possible?
questions.explanation: Boddington's definition starts from the point that when counting is not possible, estimates are needed, so statistics becomes the science of estimates and probabilities; D is correct. Bowley (A) defined it as the science of counting and of averages, and King (B) as a method of judging collective, natural and social phenomena. Option C is not linked to this definition.

questions.question: Descriptive statistics deals with:

options.a: Drawing conclusions from a sample about a population
options.d: Collection, presentation, and interpretation of data using tables, graphs, and diagrams

questions.explanation: Descriptive statistics is about collecting, presenting and interpreting data through tables, graphs, diagrams and summary measures, so D is correct. Option A describes inferential statistics, which draws conclusions about a population from a sample, and option C also belongs to inferential work. Option B is wrong because descriptive statistics mainly handles numerical data.

questions.question: Inferential statistics deals with:

options.a: Only presenting data in tables and charts
options.b: Making estimates and drawing conclusions from limited (sample) information
options.c: Calculating averages for a full population census

questions.explanation: Inferential statistics uses limited sample information to make estimates and draw conclusions about a wider population, so B is correct. Option A is the job of descriptive statistics, and option C involves a full census, where there is nothing left to infer. Option D is about how data is collected, not how conclusions are drawn.

questions.question: The mean (x-bar) is calculated as:

options.a: Middle value when data is sorted

questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean adds up all the values and divides by how many there are, x-bar = sum of x / n, so B is correct. Option A describes the median, option C the mode, and option D the range, which is a measure of spread rather than an average.

questions.question: Which measure is defined as "the middle value when data is sorted"?
questions.explanation: When data are arranged in order, the value in the middle position is the median (with an even number of values, it is the average of the two middle ones), so B is correct. Option D, the mean, is the sum divided by the count, option C, the mode, is the most frequent value, and option A, variance, measures spread.

questions.question: The Z-score formula is (X = value, mu = mean, sigma = standard deviation):
questions.explanation: A Z-score tells you how many standard deviations a value lies from the mean, so you subtract the mean and divide by the standard deviation: Z = (X - mu) / sigma, option C. Option D multiplies by sigma instead of dividing, and option A turns the correct fraction upside down. Option B ignores the standard deviation completely.

questions.question: In hypothesis testing, rejecting a TRUE null hypothesis is called:
questions.explanation: A Type I error is a false positive: you reject the null hypothesis even though it is actually true, and its probability is the significance level alpha, so C is correct. Option B, a Type II error, is the reverse mistake of failing to reject a false null hypothesis. Options A and D are not standard names for this error.

questions.question: Failing to reject a FALSE null hypothesis is called:
questions.explanation: Failing to reject a null hypothesis that is actually false is a false negative, known as a Type II error, so C is correct. Option B, the Type I error, is rejecting a true null, and option D, alpha error, is another name for that same Type I error. Option A is not a standard error type.

questions.question: Which test should be used to compare a sample mean to a known population mean when the sample is large (n >= 30) and the population standard deviation (sigma) is known?
questions.explanation: With a large sample and a known population standard deviation, the sampling distribution of the mean is treated as normal, so the Z-test (A) is used. Option D, the t-test, is for small samples where sigma is unknown, option B handles categorical data, and option C compares three or more group means.

questions.question: Which test compares the means of THREE OR MORE groups?
questions.explanation: ANOVA (analysis of variance) uses an F-test to check whether the means of three or more groups differ, so A is correct. Options B and C compare one or two means at a time, and running many separate t-tests instead would inflate the chance of a Type I error. Option D is for categorical data, not means.

questions.question: For a 95% confidence interval, the z critical value is:
questions.explanation: For a 95% confidence interval, 2.5% is left in each tail of the standard normal curve, which gives a critical value of z = 1.960, so C is correct. Option B (1.645) belongs to a 90% interval and option A (2.576) to a 99% interval, while option D (1.0) covers only about 68% of values.

questions.question: Which test is used for categorical/nominal data to test independence or goodness of fit?
questions.explanation: The chi-square test works with counts in categories, testing whether two categorical variables are independent or whether observed frequencies fit an expected pattern, so B is correct. Options A, C and D all compare means of numerical data, which is not what goodness-of-fit or independence tests do.

questions.question: A kiosk in Yaba recorded the number of recharge cards sold on 7 days: 34, 41, 29, 38, 45, 33, 40. What is the arithmetic mean number of cards sold per day (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: The mean is Sum x / n = 260 / 7 = 37.14 cards per day. Option A divides by n - 1 = 6 instead of the number of values, option C is the median (the middle value after sorting), and option B divides by 8, one more than the number of days.

questions.question: The daily absences recorded in a Lagos factory over 5 days had a mean of 14. Four of the daily figures were 12, 15, 9 and 18. What was the fifth figure?
questions.explanation: Since mean = Sum x / n, the total must be 14 x 5 = 70; the four known values add to 54, so the fifth value is 70 - 54 = 16. Option C is just the mean of the four known values, and option A wrongly assumes the missing figure must equal the mean. Option B comes from using a total of 14 x 4 = 56 instead of 14 x 5.

questions.question: The monthly sales commissions (N'000) of 9 sales agents in an Ibadan distribution firm were: 52, 47, 61, 39, 58, 44, 50, 66, 41. What is the median commission?
questions.explanation: Arranged in order the values are 39, 41, 44, 47, 50, 52, 58, 61, 66, and the middle (5th) value is 50, so the median is N50,000. Option B is the 5th value of the unsorted list, a common slip when the data are not first arranged in order. Option D is the mean, not the median, and option C is just the midpoint of the lowest and highest values.

questions.question: A bakery in Surulere recorded the number of loaves returned unsold on 8 days: 27, 35, 22, 31, 40, 29, 33, 25. What is the median number of loaves returned?
questions.explanation: With an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values after sorting: 22, 25, 27, 29, 31, 33, 35, 40 gives (29 + 31) / 2 = 30.0. Options A and B pick only one of the two middle values, and option D averages the 4th and 5th values of the unsorted list.

questions.question: The number of customer complaints received by a GTCO branch on 12 days were: 3, 5, 4, 5, 2, 6, 5, 4, 3, 5, 4, 1. What is the mode?
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often; 5 appears four times, more than any other value, so the mode is 5. Option A (4) appears only three times, option D is the largest value, and option B is the median of the data, not the mode.

questions.question: The ages of 8 apprentices in a Kano auto workshop are: 12, 15, 11, 12, 18, 15, 14, 10. Which statement about the mode is correct?

options.a: The mode is 13.375, the average of all the ages
options.b: The mode is 12 only, because it appears first
options.c: The data are bimodal, with modes 12 and 15
options.d: There is no mode, because no value appears more than twice

questions.explanation: Both 12 and 15 occur twice while every other age occurs once, so the data have two modes (bimodal). Option B is wrong because the order of appearance does not matter, option D is wrong because a value appearing twice when others appear once is still a mode, and option A gives the mean, not the mode.

questions.question: A transport firm recorded the number of breakdowns per bus in a month: 0 breakdowns (6 buses), 1 (10 buses), 2 (12 buses), 3 (8 buses), 4 (4 buses). What is the mean number of breakdowns per bus (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: For a frequency distribution, mean = Sum fx / Sum f = (0 + 10 + 24 + 24 + 16) / 40 = 74 / 40 = 1.85 breakdowns. Option D averages the values 0 to 4 and ignores the frequencies, option C divides Sum fx by the number of categories (5) instead of the total frequency, and option B divides Sum fx by Sum x.

questions.question: The daily sales (N'000) of 40 POS operators in Ikeja are grouped as: 10 to under 20 (4), 20 to under 30 (9), 30 to under 40 (15), 40 to under 50 (8), 50 to under 60 (4). Using class midpoints, what is the mean daily sales?
questions.explanation: Using midpoints 15, 25, 35, 45, 55, Sum fx = 60 + 225 + 525 + 360 + 220 = 1,390 and Sum f = 40, so the mean is 1,390 / 40 = 34.75, i.e. N34,750. Option D uses the lower class limits instead of midpoints, option A averages the midpoints without weighting by frequency, and option C divides Sum fx by the number of classes.

questions.question: The years of service of 40 staff of a Port Harcourt firm are grouped as: 0 to under 4 (5), 4 to under 8 (12), 8 to under 12 (18), 12 to under 16 (5). Using class midpoints, what is the mean length of service?
questions.explanation: Midpoints are 2, 6, 10 and 14, so Sum fx = 10 + 72 + 180 + 70 = 332 and the mean is 332 / 40 = 8.3 years. Option C uses the upper class limits instead of midpoints, option D is the simple average of the midpoints ignoring frequencies, and option A divides by the number of classes instead of Sum f.

questions.question: The scores of 50 job applicants on an aptitude test at a Lagos bank are: 20 to under 30 (6), 30 to under 40 (10), 40 to under 50 (16), 50 to under 60 (12), 60 to under 70 (6). Using Median = L + [(n/2 - CF) / f] x c, where CF is the cumulative frequency before the median class, what is the median score (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: n/2 = 25, and the cumulative frequencies 6, 16, 32 show that the 25th score lies in the 40 to under 50 class, so L = 40, CF = 16, f = 16, c = 10. Median = 40 + [(25 - 16) / 16] x 10 = 40 + 5.625 = 45.63. Option A is simply the midpoint of the median class, option C forgets to subtract CF, and option B uses a class width of 20 instead of 10.

questions.question: The weekly electricity bills (N) of 40 shops in a plaza are grouped as: 100 to under 200 (8), 200 to under 300 (14), 300 to under 400 (12), 400 to under 500 (6). Using Median = L + [(n/2 - CF) / f] x c, what is the median weekly bill (to the nearest naira)?
questions.explanation: n/2 = 20 and the cumulative frequencies are 8, 22, 34, 40, so the median class is 200 to under 300 with L = 200, CF = 8, f = 14 and c = 100. Median = 200 + [(20 - 8) / 14] x 100 = 200 + 85.71 = N286. Option D wrongly places the median in the 300 to under 400 class, option A divides by the next class's frequency (12) instead of 14, and option C uses (n + 1)/2 and forgets to subtract CF.

questions.question: The ages of 60 customers of a Lekki boutique are grouped as: 15 to under 25 (9), 25 to under 35 (18), 35 to under 45 (21), 45 to under 55 (12). Which class contains the median?
questions.explanation: The median is the (n/2)th = 30th value; cumulative frequencies are 9, 27, 48, 60, so the 30th customer falls in the 35 to under 45 class. Option D is chosen when the cumulative total of 27 is mistaken for having passed 30, while options B and C are classes far from the middle position.

questions.question: The daily output (units) of 50 tailors in Aba is grouped as: 10 to under 20 (7), 20 to under 30 (13), 30 to under 40 (19), 40 to under 50 (11). Using Mode = L + [d1 / (d1 + d2)] x c, where d1 and d2 are the differences between the modal class frequency and the frequencies of the classes before and after it, what is the mode (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: The modal class is 30 to under 40 (highest frequency 19), so L = 30, d1 = 19 - 13 = 6, d2 = 19 - 11 = 8 and c = 10. Mode = 30 + [6 / 14] x 10 = 30 + 4.29 = 34.29. Option A is just the midpoint of the modal class, option C swaps d1 and d2, and option B uses 6 / 18, adding the modal frequency differences incorrectly.

questions.question: The prices (N) charged for the same bag of rice by 6 traders at Mile 12 market are: 4,500; 3,800; 5,200; 4,100; 6,100; 3,950. What is the range of the prices?
questions.explanation: Range = Highest value - Lowest value = 6,100 - 3,800 = N2,300. Option B subtracts the first listed price from the highest (6,100 - 4,500), option D uses 3,950 as the lowest value, and option A is the mean price, which is a measure of central tendency rather than dispersion.

questions.question: Treating the data as a population, what is the variance of the weekly overtime hours of 5 security staff: 8, 12, 10, 14, 6? (Use variance = Sum(x - mean)^2 / n.)
questions.explanation: The mean is 50 / 5 = 10, the squared deviations are 4, 4, 0, 16, 16, summing to 40, so the population variance is 40 / 5 = 8.00. Option A divides by n - 1 = 4 (the sample formula), option C is the standard deviation (the square root of 8), and option D is the mean absolute deviation, which ignores squaring.

questions.question: A quality officer takes a SAMPLE of 5 cartons and counts the damaged eggs in each: 15, 22, 18, 25, 20. Using the sample formula variance = Sum(x - mean)^2 / (n - 1), what is the sample variance?
questions.explanation: The mean is 100 / 5 = 20, the squared deviations are 25, 4, 4, 25, 0, summing to 58, and the sample variance is 58 / 4 = 14.50. Option A divides by n = 5 (the population formula), option D is the sample standard deviation, and option C is the sum of squared deviations before dividing.

questions.question: The daily number of passengers carried by a keke rider over 5 days were 42, 38, 45, 35, 40. Treating these as a population, what is the standard deviation (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Mean = 200 / 5 = 40; squared deviations are 4, 4, 25, 25, 0, summing to 58; population variance = 58 / 5 = 11.6 and SD = sqrt(11.6) = 3.41. Option B stops at the variance without taking the square root, option A uses the sample formula (divide by 4), and option C takes the square root of the mean absolute deviation.

questions.question: A sample of 6 days' deliveries by a dispatch rider gave: 6, 9, 12, 7, 11, 9. Using the sample standard deviation s = sqrt[Sum(x - mean)^2 / (n - 1)], what is s (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Mean = 54 / 6 = 9; squared deviations 9, 0, 9, 4, 4, 0 sum to 26; sample variance = 26 / 5 = 5.2 and s = sqrt(5.2) = 2.28. Option A uses the population formula (divide by 6), option D is the sample variance without the square root, and option C halves the variance instead of square-rooting it.

questions.question: Two Abuja sales teams each averaged N60,000 weekly sales over 5 weeks. Team X (N'000): 60, 64, 58, 62, 56. Team Y (N'000): 40, 80, 70, 50, 60. Using population standard deviations, which conclusion is correct?

options.a: Team Y (SD about 14.14) is more consistent than Team X (SD about 2.83)
options.b: Both teams are equally consistent because their means are equal
options.c: Team X (SD about 8.00) is less consistent than Team Y (SD about 7.07)
options.d: Team X (SD about 2.83) is more consistent than Team Y (SD about 14.14)

questions.explanation: Team X has squared deviations summing to 40, so SD = sqrt(40/5) = 2.83, while Team Y's sum to 1,000, giving SD = sqrt(200) = 14.14; the smaller SD means Team X's sales vary less from week to week. Option A reverses the interpretation (a larger SD means less consistency), and option B wrongly assumes equal means imply equal spread.

questions.question: The standard deviation of the monthly fuel cost of a logistics firm is N3,500. What is the variance of the monthly fuel cost?
questions.explanation: Standard deviation is the square root of the variance, so the variance is the SD squared: 3,500^2 = 12,250,000 (in squared naira). Option A takes the square root instead of squaring, while options D and B halve or double the SD, which has no statistical meaning.

questions.question: A Lagos supermarket's daily revenue has a mean of N250,000 and a standard deviation of N30,000. What is the coefficient of variation?
questions.explanation: CV = (SD / mean) x 100% = (30,000 / 250,000) x 100% = 12.0%. Option D inverts the ratio (mean / SD), option B subtracts the CV from 100%, and option A simply subtracts the SD from the mean, which is not a relative measure.

questions.question: Share P has a mean monthly return of 30 kobo with SD 4.5 kobo; Share Q has a mean of 75 kobo with SD 9 kobo. Using the coefficient of variation, which share is relatively riskier?

options.a: Share P, CV = 15.0% against 12.0% for Q
options.b: Share Q, because its SD of 9 kobo is larger
options.c: Share Q, CV = 8.3% against 6.7% for P
options.d: Both are equally risky, CV = 15.0% each

questions.explanation: CV measures dispersion relative to the mean: P = 4.5 / 30 x 100% = 15.0% and Q = 9 / 75 x 100% = 12.0%, so P is relatively riskier even though its SD is smaller. Option B compares raw SDs, which is misleading when means differ, and option C inverts the CV formula.

questions.question: The daily production (crates) of a soft-drink line over 5 days was 20, 25, 30, 25, 25. Using the population standard deviation, what is the coefficient of variation (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Mean = 125 / 5 = 25; squared deviations 25, 0, 25, 0, 0 sum to 50, so SD = sqrt(50/5) = 3.162 and CV = 3.162 / 25 x 100% = 12.65%. Option C uses the variance (10) instead of the SD, option A uses the sample SD (divide by 4), and option B inverts the ratio.

questions.question: For a population of 10 monthly sales figures (N'000), Sum x = 80 and Sum x^2 = 700. Using variance = (Sum x^2 / n) - (mean)^2, what is the population variance?
questions.explanation: The mean is 80 / 10 = 8, so variance = 700 / 10 - 8^2 = 70 - 64 = 6. Option A forgets to subtract the squared mean, option B applies the sample (n - 1) version, and option C subtracts the mean rather than the squared mean.

questions.question: A hotel recorded the number of rooms cleaned per hour by 10 cleaners: 1 room (2 cleaners), 2 rooms (5), 3 rooms (2), 4 rooms (1). Treating this as a population, what is the variance (Sum f(x - mean)^2 / Sum f)?
questions.explanation: The mean is Sum fx / Sum f = (2 + 10 + 6 + 4) / 10 = 2.2; Sum f(x - 2.2)^2 = 2(1.44) + 5(0.04) + 2(0.64) + 1(3.24) = 7.6, so variance = 7.6 / 10 = 0.76. Option D ignores the frequencies, option B is the standard deviation, and option C divides by Sum f - 1 = 9.

questions.question: The monthly salaries of 20 clerks have a mean of N85,000 and a standard deviation of N6,000. If every clerk receives a flat increase of N5,000, what are the new mean and standard deviation?
questions.explanation: Adding the same amount to every value shifts the whole distribution, so the mean rises by N5,000 to N90,000, but each deviation from the mean is unchanged, so the SD stays at N6,000. Option C wrongly adds the increase to the SD, option B ignores the increase altogether, and option D scales the SD in proportion to the mean.

questions.question: Scores on a bank's recruitment test are normally distributed with mean 65 and standard deviation 8. What is the z-score of a candidate who scored 78?
questions.explanation: z = (X - mu) / sigma = (78 - 65) / 8 = 1.625, so the candidate is 1.625 standard deviations above the mean. Option D divides by the variance (64) instead of the SD, option B forgets to subtract the mean, and option A multiplies by sigma instead of dividing.

questions.question: The time taken to serve customers at a fast-food outlet is normally distributed with mean 50 seconds and SD 5 seconds. What is the z-score for a service time of 42 seconds?
questions.explanation: z = (42 - 50) / 5 = -1.6; the negative sign shows the time is below the mean. Option D drops the sign, option C divides by the variance (25), and option B divides the value by the mean, which is not a z-score.

questions.question: Weekly sales of a product are normally distributed with mean 120 units and SD 16 units. A store manager wants the sales level that is 1.5 standard deviations above the mean. What is it?
questions.explanation: Rearranging z = (X - mu) / sigma gives X = mu + z sigma = 120 + 1.5 x 16 = 144 units. Option A adds z without multiplying by sigma, option C multiplies the mean by 1.5, and option D subtracts, giving the value 1.5 SD below the mean.

questions.question: Daily cash withdrawals at an ATM are normally distributed with mean N2,400,000 and SD N300,000. About what percentage of days have withdrawals between N2,100,000 and N2,700,000?
questions.explanation: N2,100,000 and N2,700,000 are exactly one SD (N300,000) below and above the mean, and the empirical rule puts about 68% of observations within +/-1 SD. Option A is the figure for +/-2 SD and option C for +/-3 SD, while option D is only the half on one side of the mean.

questions.question: The weights of bags of cement are normally distributed with mean 50 kg and SD 0.4 kg. Using the empirical rule, about what percentage of bags weigh MORE than 50.8 kg?
questions.explanation: 50.8 kg is 2 SD above the mean; about 95% of bags lie within +/-2 SD, leaving 5% in the two tails, so about 2.5% lie above 50.8 kg by symmetry. Option D forgets to split the 5% between the two tails, option C is the tail beyond 1 SD, and option B is the share between the mean and +2 SD.

questions.question: A firm employs 2,000 machine operators whose productivity scores are normally distributed with mean 70 and SD 6. Using the empirical rule, about how many operators score between 52 and 88?
questions.explanation: 52 and 88 are 3 SD (18 points) below and above the mean, so about 99.7% of operators lie in this range: 0.997 x 2,000 = 1,994. Option A uses 95% (the +/-2 SD figure), option C uses 68% (the +/-1 SD figure), and option B assumes every operator falls within the range.

questions.question: A bottling plant fills sachet water with a process mean of 500 ml and a process standard deviation of 4 ml. Using limits set at 3 standard deviations, what is the Upper Control Limit?
questions.explanation: UCL = mean + 3 sigma = 500 + 3(4) = 512 ml. Option C uses only 1 SD, option B uses 2 SD, and option D multiplies the mean by 3 instead of adding 3 standard deviations.

questions.question: The average length of steel rods produced by a Kaduna mill is 120 cm with a process standard deviation of 1.5 cm. Using 3-sigma control limits, what is the Lower Control Limit?
questions.explanation: LCL = mean - 3 sigma = 120 - 3(1.5) = 115.5 cm. Option B subtracts only one SD, option A subtracts two SDs, and option C is the Upper Control Limit, not the lower one.

questions.question: A process has mean 80 g and standard deviation 2 g, with 3-sigma control limits. Sample means for five hours were 83.5 g, 78.0 g, 86.4 g, 75.2 g and 81.9 g. Which hour signals that the process may be out of control?
questions.explanation: The limits are 80 +/- 3(2), i.e. LCL = 74 g and UCL = 86 g, and only 86.4 g lies outside them, so it signals a possible special cause to investigate. Options A and B lie more than 1 SD from the mean but are still inside the 3-sigma limits, and option C is close to the mean.

questions.question: A survey of 36 households in Ikorodu found mean monthly spending on transport of N4,200. The population standard deviation is N600. What is the 95% confidence interval for the mean? (CI = mean +/- z x sigma / sqrt n.)
questions.explanation: The margin is 1.96 x 600 / sqrt(36) = 1.96 x 100 = N196, so the interval is 4,200 +/- 196, i.e. N4,004 to N4,396. Option D uses the 90% value 1.645, option C divides by n instead of sqrt n, and option B forgets to divide sigma by sqrt n at all.

questions.question: A sample of 25 customers spent an average of 52 minutes in a shopping mall; the population SD is 10 minutes. What is the UPPER limit of the 99% confidence interval for the mean time (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Upper limit = mean + z x sigma / sqrt n = 52 + 2.576 x 10 / 5 = 52 + 5.152 = 57.15 minutes. Option C uses the 95% value 1.96, option D is the lower limit, and option A divides sigma by n instead of sqrt n.

questions.question: For a 90% confidence interval for the mean daily sales of a supermarket chain, a sample of 64 days is used and the population SD is N800. What is the margin of error (z x sigma / sqrt n) to 2 decimal places?
questions.explanation: Margin of error = 1.645 x 800 / sqrt(64) = 1.645 x 100 = N164.50. Option B uses the 95% value 1.96, option C uses the 99% value 2.576, and option A divides by 64 instead of its square root.

questions.question: A marketing officer recorded radio adverts per week (x) and sales in N'000 (y): (1, 10), (2, 14), (3, 15), (4, 19), (5, 22). What is Sum xy?
questions.explanation: Sum xy multiplies each pair and adds: 10 + 28 + 45 + 76 + 110 = 269. Option A is Sum x times Sum y (15 x 80), which is a different term in the formula, option C adds Sum x^2 and Sum y^2, and option B merely adds Sum x and Sum y.

questions.question: Using the same data, (1, 10), (2, 14), (3, 15), (4, 19), (5, 22), where n = 5, Sum x = 15, Sum y = 80, Sum xy = 269, Sum x^2 = 55 and Sum y^2 = 1,366, what is Pearson's correlation coefficient r (to 3 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: r = [5(269) - 15(80)] / sqrt{[5(55) - 15^2][5(1,366) - 80^2]} = 145 / sqrt(50 x 430) = 145 / 146.63 = 0.989, a very strong positive relationship. Option B is r^2 (the coefficient of determination), option D is the regression slope b (145 / 50), and option C forgets to take the square root of the denominator.

questions.question: A phone dealer in Computer Village records the price of a handset in N'0,000 (x) and weekly units sold (y): (3, 40), (5, 36), (7, 31), (9, 27), (11, 21). Given n = 5, Sum x = 35, Sum y = 155, Sum xy = 991, Sum x^2 = 285, Sum y^2 = 5,027, what is Pearson's r (to 3 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Numerator = 5(991) - 35(155) = -470; denominator = sqrt{[5(285) - 35^2][5(5,027) - 155^2]} = sqrt(200 x 1,110) = 471.17; r = -470 / 471.17 = -0.998, a very strong negative relationship (higher price, fewer sales). Option A drops the negative sign, option B is r^2, which can never be negative, and option C is the regression slope b, not r.

questions.question: For two variables, Sum(x - x-bar)(y - y-bar) = 84, Sum(x - x-bar)^2 = 60 and Sum(y - y-bar)^2 = 196. Using r = Sum[(x - x-bar)(y - y-bar)] / sqrt{Sum(x - x-bar)^2 x Sum(y - y-bar)^2}, what is r (to 3 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: r = 84 / sqrt(60 x 196) = 84 / 108.44 = 0.775, a strong positive relationship. Option B divides only by Sum(y - y-bar)^2, option D is 84 / 60, which is the regression slope b rather than r, and option A adds the two square roots instead of multiplying inside one root.

questions.question: The correlation between training hours and productivity at a Lagos factory is r = 0.85. What percentage of the variation in productivity is explained by training hours?
questions.explanation: The coefficient of determination is r^2 = 0.85^2 = 0.7225, so 72.25% of the variation in productivity is explained by training hours. Option A uses r itself, option B takes the square root of r, and option D is simply 1 - r, which has no meaning here.

questions.question: A regression of weekly demand on price gives y-hat = 900 - 12x, with coefficient of determination r^2 = 0.64. What is the correlation coefficient r?
questions.explanation: r is the square root of r^2, so |r| = sqrt(0.64) = 0.80, and r takes the sign of the slope; since b = -12 is negative, r = -0.80. Option C ignores the sign of the slope, option A confuses r with r^2, and option D squares 0.64 instead of square-rooting it.

questions.question: A Lagos eatery recorded promotion spending x (N'000) and sales y (N'000) over 5 weeks: (2, 15), (4, 19), (6, 26), (8, 30), (10, 35). With n = 5, Sum x = 30, Sum y = 125, Sum xy = 852 and Sum x^2 = 220, what is the regression slope b?
questions.explanation: b = [n Sum xy - Sum x Sum y] / [n Sum x^2 - (Sum x)^2] = [5(852) - 30(125)] / [5(220) - 30^2] = 510 / 200 = 2.55. Option A forgets to subtract (Sum x)^2 in the denominator, option C divides Sum xy by Sum x^2 directly, and option D is the correlation coefficient, not the slope.

questions.question: For the same eatery data (x-bar = 6, y-bar = 25) the slope is b = 2.55. What is the intercept a of the regression line y-hat = a + bx?
questions.explanation: a = y-bar - b x-bar = 25 - 2.55(6) = 25 - 15.3 = 9.70. Option D adds instead of subtracting, option A swaps x-bar and y-bar, and option C subtracts b without multiplying it by x-bar.

questions.question: Using the regression line y-hat = 9.7 + 2.55x, where x is weekly promotion spending (N'000) and y is weekly sales (N'000), what sales are predicted when N12,000 is spent on promotion?
questions.explanation: Substituting x = 12: y-hat = 9.7 + 2.55(12) = 9.7 + 30.6 = 40.3, i.e. N40,300. Option A multiplies both a and b by x, option D leaves out the intercept, and option C multiplies the intercept rather than the slope by x.

questions.question: A recruitment agency recorded years of experience x and monthly pay y (N'0,000) for 5 staff: (2, 8), (3, 11), (5, 14), (6, 17), (9, 25). Given Sum x = 25, Sum y = 75, Sum xy = 446 and Sum x^2 = 155, use y-hat = a + bx (unrounded b and a) to predict the pay of someone with 10 years' experience (to 2 decimal places).
questions.explanation: b = [5(446) - 25(75)] / [5(155) - 625] = 355 / 150 = 2.3667 and a = 15 - 2.3667(5) = 3.1667, so y-hat = 3.1667 + 2.3667(10) = 26.83 (about N268,300). Option C ignores the intercept, option A predicts for x = 12 instead of 10, and option B adds 10 to a without multiplying by b.

questions.question: A firm estimates y-hat = 45 + 3.2x, where y is monthly sales (N'000) and x is the number of sales calls made. What does the model predict will happen to sales if a representative makes 5 MORE calls than before?
questions.explanation: The slope b = 3.2 is the change in y for each one-unit increase in x, so 5 extra calls raise predicted sales by 5 x 3.2 = 16 thousand, i.e. N16,000; the intercept does not affect a change. Option D adds the intercept to the change, option B is the effect of only one extra call, and option A adds b to the intercept.

questions.question: Two judges ranked 6 entries in a Lagos small-business pitch competition. Judge 1: A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4, E=5, F=6. Judge 2: A=2, B=1, C=4, D=3, E=6, F=5. Using Spearman's R = 1 - 6 Sum d^2 / [n(n^2 - 1)], what is R (to 3 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: Every pair of ranks differs by 1, so Sum d^2 = 6 and R = 1 - 6(6) / [6(35)] = 1 - 36 / 210 = 0.829, a strong agreement between the judges. Option D uses n^2 + 1 instead of n^2 - 1, option B leaves out the 6 in the numerator, and option A forgets to subtract from 1.

questions.question: Five provision shops recorded weekly sales of a detergent (cartons) and their selling prices (N): Shop 1 (45, 700), Shop 2 (38, 820), Shop 3 (52, 650), Shop 4 (30, 900), Shop 5 (41, 760). Ranking each variable from highest = 1, what is Spearman's rank correlation R = 1 - 6 Sum d^2 / [n(n^2 - 1)]?
questions.explanation: Sales ranks are 2, 4, 1, 5, 3 and price ranks are 4, 2, 5, 1, 3, giving d^2 values 4, 4, 16, 16, 0, so Sum d^2 = 40 and R = 1 - 240 / 120 = -1.00, a perfect negative rank correlation (higher price, lower sales). Option B drops the sign, while options C and D would need Sum d^2 of 20 and 30 respectively.

questions.question: In ranking 10 branch managers on two performance criteria, an HR officer finds Sum d^2 = 33. Using R = 1 - 6 Sum d^2 / [n(n^2 - 1)], what is Spearman's rank correlation (to 2 decimal places)?
questions.explanation: R = 1 - 6(33) / [10(100 - 1)] = 1 - 198 / 990 = 0.80, a strong positive agreement between the two criteria. Option D uses n(n - 1) in the denominator, option B forgets to subtract the fraction from 1, and option C leaves out the 6.

questions.question: For the daily sales of 40 roadside vendors, the first quartile is N3,200, the median is N4,500 and the third quartile is N6,100. What is the interquartile range?
questions.explanation: IQR = Q3 - Q1 = 6,100 - 3,200 = N2,900, the spread of the middle 50% of the data. Option C is the median minus Q1 and option A is Q3 minus the median, each covering only a quarter of the data, while option B averages Q1 and Q3.

questions.question: A company has 20 field staff in Lagos with a mean monthly allowance of N45,000 and 30 field staff in Abuja with a mean of N55,000. What is the mean allowance of all 50 staff combined?
questions.explanation: The combined mean weights each group mean by its size: (20 x 45,000 + 30 x 55,000) / 50 = 2,550,000 / 50 = N51,000. Option B is the simple average of the two means, which ignores the different group sizes, option A attaches the weights to the wrong groups, and option D has no valid basis.

questions.question: The daily earnings (N'00) of 7 traders are 60, 65, 70, 72, 75, 80 and 450. Which measure best represents typical earnings, and what is its value?
questions.explanation: The extreme value 450 pulls the mean up to 124.57, far above what six of the seven traders earn, whereas the median (the 4th sorted value, 72) is not affected by the outlier. Option B is distorted by the extreme value, option C is wrong because no value repeats, and option A is a measure of dispersion, not of typical earnings.

questions.question: A student recorded her weekly spending on food (N) over 6 weeks: 1,200; 950; 1,430; 1,100; 870; 1,310. What was her mean weekly spending (to the nearest naira)?
questions.explanation: Mean = Sum x / n = 6,860 / 6 = N1,143. Option C divides by 5 instead of 6, option B is the median (average of the two middle values), and option A divides by 7, one more than the number of weeks.

questions.question: Ada scored 72 in Accounting (class mean 60, SD 8) and 84 in Economics (class mean 75, SD 5). Using z-scores, in which subject did she perform better relative to her classmates?

options.b: Accounting, because its gap of 12 marks above the mean is larger
options.c: Both equally, because each score is above its class mean

questions.explanation: z standardises each score: Accounting z = (72 - 60) / 8 = 1.50 and Economics z = (84 - 75) / 5 = 1.80, so Economics is the stronger relative performance. Option B compares raw gaps from the mean and ignores the different spreads, option C ignores how far above the mean each score is in SD units, and option A divides by the variances instead of the SDs.

questions.question: Monthly phone bills of a company's staff are normally distributed with mean N8,000 and SD N1,200. Within which range do about 95% of the bills lie?
questions.explanation: About 95% of a normal distribution lies within +/-2 SD of the mean: 8,000 +/- 2(1,200) gives N5,600 to N10,400. Option A is the +/-1 SD range (about 68%), option D is the +/-3 SD range (about 99.7%), and option B wrongly takes 12% of the mean on each side.

questions.question: For 5 branches, the number of staff (x) and customer satisfaction scores (y) are: (2, 30), (4, 26), (5, 33), (7, 29), (8, 35). Given n = 5, Sum x = 26, Sum y = 153, Sum xy = 812, Sum x^2 = 158 and Sum y^2 = 4,731, what is Pearson's r and how is it best described?

options.a: r = 0.24, no linear relationship at all

questions.explanation: r = [5(812) - 26(153)] / sqrt{[5(158) - 26^2][5(4,731) - 153^2]} = 82 / sqrt(114 x 246) = 82 / 167.46 = 0.49, which falls in the 0.4 to 0.6 band for a moderate positive correlation. Option D gives the right value but overstates its strength, option B gets the sign wrong, and option A reports r^2 and wrongly calls it no relationship.

questions.question: King defined statistics as:

options.a: The method of judging collective, natural and social phenomena from the results of analysis, enumeration or collection of estimates
options.b: The science of estimates and probabilities, used when counting is not possible
options.c: The collection, presentation and interpretation of data in tables, graphs and diagrams
options.d: The science of counting and the science of averages

questions.explanation: King's definition presents statistics as a method of judging collective, natural and social phenomena from the results of analysis, enumeration or estimates. Option D is Bowley's definition, option B is Boddington's, and option C describes descriptive statistics, which is a branch rather than a definition of the whole subject.

questions.question: A market researcher in Onitsha surveys 200 shoppers and uses the results to estimate the average spending of all shoppers in the city. Which branch of statistics is she using?
questions.explanation: Drawing conclusions about a whole population from limited sample information is inferential statistics. Option A, descriptive statistics, only collects, presents and interprets the data in hand without generalising beyond it, while options B and C borrow labels from model classification and are not branches of statistics.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a measure of dispersion?
questions.explanation: The median is a measure of central tendency: it locates the middle of the data rather than describing spread. The interquartile range (option D), coefficient of variation (option A) and standard deviation (option C) all measure how widely values are scattered.

questions.question: The spread of the middle 50% of a data set, found by subtracting the first quartile from the third quartile, is called the:
questions.explanation: The interquartile range is Q3 - Q1 and measures the spread of the middle half of the data, so it is not distorted by extreme values. Option D, the range, uses the highest and lowest values, option B averages squared deviations from the mean, and option C expresses the SD as a percentage of the mean.

questions.question: The coefficient of variation, CV = (SD / mean) x 100%, is mainly used to:

options.a: Locate the middle value of a data set
options.b: Compare the relative variability of data sets with different means or units
options.c: Set the upper and lower limits on a control chart
options.d: Measure the strength of the linear relationship between two variables

questions.explanation: Because CV expresses the SD as a percentage of the mean, it measures relative dispersion and allows fair comparison of risk or consistency when means or units differ. Option D describes correlation, option A describes the median, and option C describes control limits, which use the mean plus or minus 3 SD.

questions.question: Which of the following is a property of the normal distribution?

options.a: The mean is always greater than the median
options.b: It is skewed to the right
options.c: The total area under the curve equals 1 (100%)
options.d: Only 50% of observations lie within 3 standard deviations of the mean

questions.explanation: The normal curve is a probability distribution, so the total area under it is 1 (100%); it is also symmetrical and bell-shaped. Option A is wrong because the mean, median and mode coincide, option B contradicts its symmetry, and option D is wrong because about 99.7% lie within 3 SD.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of the normal distribution?

options.a: It has a long tail on one side because extreme values are more common there
options.c: Its mean, median and mode coincide at the centre
options.d: About 68% of observations lie within one standard deviation of the mean

questions.explanation: The normal distribution is symmetrical, so neither tail is longer than the other; a long tail on one side describes a skewed distribution. Options B, C and D are all genuine features: the bell shape, the coinciding mean, median and mode, and the 68% part of the empirical rule.

questions.question: A quality manager at a Lagos paint factory tests H0: 'the mean fill volume is 4 litres'. In reality the mean IS 4 litres, but the test leads her to reject H0. What has occurred?
questions.explanation: Rejecting a null hypothesis that is actually true is a Type I error (a false positive), whose probability is alpha. Option B, a Type II error, would be failing to reject a false H0, option D is wrong because a true H0 was rejected, and option C concerns how a sample is drawn, not the test decision.

questions.question: A bank tests H0: 'the new app has no effect on average transaction time'. The app actually does reduce transaction time, but the test fails to reject H0. This is:
questions.explanation: Failing to reject a null hypothesis that is actually false is a Type II error (a false negative), whose probability is beta. Option D, a Type I error, is rejecting a true H0, option C is the statement the test tries to support (the effect exists), and option A relates to confidence intervals.

questions.question: In hypothesis testing, the null hypothesis (H0) is:

options.a: The range of values within which the population mean is expected to lie
options.b: The default assumption that no effect or difference exists
options.c: The claim the researcher is trying to prove
options.d: The probability of rejecting a true hypothesis

questions.explanation: H0 is the default position of 'no effect or no difference' that the test tries to find evidence against. Option C is the alternative hypothesis H1, option D describes alpha, the probability of a Type I error, and option A describes a confidence interval.

questions.question: A researcher wants to test whether the mean weight of 12 sampled bags of garri differs from 50 kg. The population standard deviation is unknown. Which test is appropriate?
questions.explanation: With a small sample (n < 30) and an unknown population SD, the t-test is used. Option D, the Z-test, needs a large sample with sigma known, option C is for categorical or nominal data, and option A compares the means of three or more groups.

questions.question: An HR officer wants to test whether job grade (junior, middle, senior) is independent of preferred pension provider (three named providers), using counts of staff in each category. Which test should be used?
questions.explanation: Counts of staff falling into named categories are categorical (nominal) data, and the chi-square test checks independence or goodness of fit for such data. Options B and C test means of numerical data, and option D measures linear association between two numerical variables.

questions.question: A retailer compares the mean daily sales of four branches (Ikeja, Yaba, Ajah and Ikorodu) to see whether any differ significantly. Which test is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: ANOVA is designed to compare the means of three or more groups at once. Option C is for categorical counts, option D handles only two groups at a time, and option A measures association between two ranked variables rather than differences in means.

questions.question: A study finds a strong positive correlation between the number of generators sold and the number of mosquito nets sold in Lagos markets each month. Both rise in the rainy season. What is the most appropriate conclusion?

options.a: The correlation must be a calculation error because the products are unrelated
options.b: A third factor (the season) may drive both, so correlation alone does not show that one causes the other
options.c: Mosquito net sales cause generator sales
options.d: Generator sales cause mosquito net sales

questions.explanation: Correlation is not causation: a lurking variable such as the season can make two series move together without one causing the other. Options D and C assume a causal direction the data cannot prove, and option A is wrong because a genuine correlation can exist even between unrelated products.

questions.question: An economist studies the relationship between maize yield and fertiliser use while holding rainfall constant. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Partial correlation studies two variables while holding the other variables constant. Option C, multiple correlation, would study yield against fertiliser and rainfall together, option B, total correlation, considers all variables without holding any constant, and option D describes the shape of a relationship, not which variables are controlled.

questions.question: A correlation coefficient of r = 0.5 between advertising spend and footfall is best described as:
questions.explanation: Values of r between 0.4 and 0.6 indicate moderate positive correlation. Option C needs r of about 0.7 to 0.9, option B needs r = +1, and option D would need a negative value of r.

questions.question: On a scatter diagram of price against quantity demanded for bread, all the points lie exactly on a straight line sloping downwards. The correlation coefficient is:
questions.explanation: Points lying exactly on a downward-sloping straight line show a perfect negative linear relationship, r = -1. Option A is an exact upward-sloping line, option B means no linear relationship, and option D would show scattered points with only a moderate downward trend.

questions.question: A control chart for the weight of noodle packs shows every point inside the UCL and LCL, scattered randomly around the centre line. What should the production manager conclude?

options.a: The control limits must have been set at 1 standard deviation
options.b: The process is out of control and must be stopped immediately
options.c: The process appears to be in statistical control, with only random variation present
options.d: The process mean has shifted upwards

questions.explanation: Points within the 3-sigma limits with no pattern suggest only random (common-cause) variation, so the process is in control. Option B applies only when points fall outside the limits, option A has no basis in the chart pattern, and option D would show up as a run of points drifting above the centre line or crossing the UCL.

questions.question: The 'average of the squared deviations of the values from their mean' defines the:
questions.explanation: Variance is Sum(x - mean)^2 divided by n (or n - 1 for a sample), i.e. the average squared deviation. Option D, the standard deviation, is its square root, option A averages absolute (not squared) deviations, and option B divides the SD by the mean.

questions.question: The critical path in a project network is:

options.a: The path with the lowest total cost
options.b: The longest path through the network
options.c: The shortest path through the network
options.d: The path with the most activities

questions.explanation: The critical path is the longest path through the network, and it sets the minimum time needed to complete the project, so any delay on it delays the whole project. The shortest path (C) has spare time (float), cost (A) does not define the critical path, and the path with the most activities (D) is not necessarily the longest in time.

questions.question: Total float on the critical path is always:
questions.explanation: Activities on the critical path have no spare time, so their total float is zero; delaying any of them delays the whole project. Positive float (A) belongs to non-critical activities, and float is never equal to the whole project duration (D).

questions.question: The EOQ formula is:
questions.explanation: EOQ = square root of (2DS / H), where D is annual demand, S is the ordering cost per order and H is the holding cost per unit per year. Option B forgets the square root, and option D turns the terms inside the square root the wrong way round.

questions.question: In the EOQ model, S represents:
questions.explanation: In EOQ = square root of (2DS / H), S is the cost of placing one order, such as processing and delivery charges. Annual demand (A) is D, the holding cost per unit (B) is H, and safety stock (D) is not part of the basic EOQ formula.

questions.question: In the basic EOQ model, when the order quantity equals the Economic Order Quantity, total annual ordering cost:

options.b: Always equals total annual holding cost
options.c: Is always greater than holding cost
options.d: Has no relationship with holding cost

questions.explanation: The EOQ is the point where the falling ordering-cost curve meets the rising holding-cost curve, so the two annual costs are exactly equal there and their total is lowest. This equality is a handy check on any EOQ calculation. Option C would mean you are ordering too often (too small a quantity), and Option A is impossible because every order placed costs something.

questions.question: The Reorder Point (ROP) is calculated as:
questions.explanation: The reorder point is the stock level at which a new order must be placed so that stock lasts until delivery, so it equals daily demand multiplied by the lead time in days. Option C gives the number of orders per year, and Option A gives the average inventory held under EOQ, not the reorder level.

questions.question: In linear programming, the objective function is:

options.b: The function to be maximised or minimised

questions.explanation: The objective function states the goal of the model, such as maximising profit or minimising cost, in terms of the decision variables. Option A confuses it with the constraints, which limit the resources available, and Option C is wrong because in linear programming the objective function is linear by definition.

questions.question: Non-negativity restrictions in linear programming require that:

options.a: Decision variables can be any real number
options.d: Only the objective function must be positive

questions.explanation: Non-negativity restrictions say each decision variable must be zero or positive, because a firm cannot produce a negative number of units. Option B reverses the sign, and Option A would allow meaningless negative production quantities.

questions.question: Which technique would best help a project manager determine the minimum time to complete a multi-activity production schedule?
questions.explanation: The Critical Path Method maps all activities and their dependencies and finds the longest path through the network, which is the minimum time needed to finish the whole project. Option B, linear programming, is for allocating limited resources to maximise or minimise an objective, and Option A, EOQ, is for inventory ordering decisions.

questions.question: An activity with zero total float lies on the:
questions.explanation: Float is the time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project, and activities on the critical path have none, so zero float marks a critical activity. Option A is wrong because the shortest path is the one with the most spare time, not the least.

questions.question: Holding (carrying) cost in inventory management includes:

options.b: Cost of storage, insurance, and spoilage

questions.explanation: Holding cost is the cost of keeping stock, such as warehousing, insurance, spoilage and the money tied up in inventory. Option A is the ordering cost, which is the other cost the EOQ model balances, while Options C and D are not inventory carrying costs.

questions.question: A feasible region in linear programming represents:

options.b: The set of all solutions that satisfy every constraint

questions.explanation: The feasible region is the area on the graph containing every combination of decision variables that satisfies all the constraints at once, including non-negativity. Option C is too narrow: the optimal solution is just one point (usually a corner point) inside this region, and Option D is a separate line used to find that point.

questions.question: In network analysis (CPM), the critical path is:
